claim: Mutations in PIK3CA and other PI3K-AKT pathway components have been associated with cancer and a wide spectrum of brain and body overgrowth.
source: Mutations in the catalytic subunit of phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PIK3CA) and other PI3K-AKT pathway components have been associated with cancer and a wide spectrum of brain and body overgrowth.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature establishing the association between PIK3CA mutations and cancer/overgrowth disorders.

claim: The phenotypic spectrum of PIK3CA-related segmental overgrowth includes bilateral dysplastic megalencephaly, hemimegalencephaly and focal cortical dysplasia.
source: In the brain, the phenotypic spectrum of PIK3CA-related segmental overgrowth includes bilateral dysplastic megalencephaly, hemimegalencephaly and focal cortical dysplasia, the most common cause of intractable pediatric epilepsy.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge about PIK3CA-related brain disorders.

claim: Focal cortical dysplasia is the most common cause of intractable pediatric epilepsy.
source: In the brain, the phenotypic spectrum of PIK3CA-related segmental overgrowth includes bilateral dysplastic megalencephaly, hemimegalencephaly and focal cortical dysplasia, the most common cause of intractable pediatric epilepsy.
evidence: This claim is supported by established medical knowledge about focal cortical dysplasia.

claim: Mouse models expressing H1047R and E545K Pik3ca mutations in developing neural progenitors accurately recapitulate all key human pathological features including brain enlargement, cortical malformation, hydrocephalus and epilepsy.
source: We generated mouse models expressing the most common activating Pik3ca mutations (H1047R and E545K) in developing neural progenitors. These accurately recapitulate all the key human pathological features including brain enlargement, cortical malformation, hydrocephalus and epilepsy, with phenotypic severity dependent on the mutant allele and its time of activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript showing these phenotypes in the mouse models.

claim: Phenotypic severity in Pik3ca mouse models is dependent on the mutant allele and its time of activation.
source: These accurately recapitulate all the key human pathological features including brain enlargement, cortical malformation, hydrocephalus and epilepsy, with phenotypic severity dependent on the mutant allele and its time of activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing different alleles and activation times throughout the manuscript.

claim: Underlying mechanisms of Pik3ca-related brain overgrowth include increased proliferation, cell size and altered white matter.
source: Underlying mechanisms include increased proliferation, cell size and altered white matter.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figures 2-6 showing these cellular mechanisms.

claim: Acute 1 hr-suppression of PI3K signaling has dramatic anti-epileptic benefit despite the ongoing presence of dysplasia.
source: Notably, we demonstrate that acute 1 hr-suppression of PI3K signaling despite the ongoing presence of dysplasia has dramatic anti-epileptic benefit.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing BKM120 treatment effects on seizures in Figure 7.

claim: PI3K inhibitors offer a promising new avenue for effective anti-epileptic therapy for intractable pediatric epilepsy patients.
source: Thus PI3K inhibitors offer a promising new avenue for effective anti-epileptic therapy for intractable pediatric epilepsy patients.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental data showing efficacy of BKM120 in mouse models.

claim: Activating mutations in genes of PI3K-AKT signaling pathway, especially PIK3CA, have long been linked to cancer.
source: Activating mutations in genes of PI3K-AKT signaling pathway, especially PIK3CA, encoding the catalytic p110α isoform of the PI3K complex, have long been linked to cancer (Cheung and Testa, 2013; Engelman, 2009; Hennessy et al., 2005; Iwabuchi et al., 1995; Samuels and Waldman, 2011; Gymnopoulos et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Germline and mosaic mutations of PIK3CA and other pathway genes cause a wide range of brain and body overgrowth disorders.
source: Germline and mosaic mutations of PIK3CA and other pathway genes also cause a wide range of brain and body overgrowth disorders; all anomalies caused by somatic PIK3CA mutations are now collectively termed PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum (PROS) (Keppler-Noreuil et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature establishing PROS classification.

claim: All anomalies caused by somatic PIK3CA mutations are collectively termed PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum (PROS).
source: Germline and mosaic mutations of PIK3CA and other pathway genes also cause a wide range of brain and body overgrowth disorders; all anomalies caused by somatic PIK3CA mutations are now collectively termed PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum (PROS) (Keppler-Noreuil et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the literature defining PROS.

claim: Three strongly activating PIK3CA mutations found most commonly in cancer result in severe segmental cortical dysplasia (SEGCD).
source: Three strongly activating PIK3CA mutations found most commonly in cancer (hotspot mutations) result in severe segmental cortical dysplasia (SEGCD), which includes bilateral dysplastic megalencephaly (MEG), hemimegalencephaly (HMEG) and focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) types 2a/2b (Lee et al., 2012; D'Gama et al., 2015; Conway et al., 2007; Jansen et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: SEGCD includes bilateral dysplastic megalencephaly (MEG), hemimegalencephaly (HMEG) and focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) types 2a/2b.
source: Three strongly activating PIK3CA mutations found most commonly in cancer (hotspot mutations) result in severe segmental cortical dysplasia (SEGCD), which includes bilateral dysplastic megalencephaly (MEG), hemimegalencephaly (HMEG) and focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) types 2a/2b (Lee et al., 2012; D'Gama et al., 2015; Conway et al., 2007; Jansen et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature defining SEGCD subtypes.

claim: Other PIK3CA mutations resulting in intermediate or weak activation cause MEG or MEG with polymicrogyria (MEG-PMG) as part of the MEG-capillary malformation syndrome (MCAP).
source: Other mutations, resulting in intermediate or weak PIK3CA activation, cause MEG or MEG with polymicrogyria (MEG-PMG) as part of the MEG-capillary malformation syndrome (MCAP) (Conway et al., 2007; Mirzaa et al., 2012; Rivière et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Developmental features of PIK3CA-related brain disorders include cortical malformations, hydrocephalus, Chiari malformation, intellectual disability, autism and epilepsy.
source: Developmental features of these brain disorders include cortical malformations, hydrocephalus, Chiari malformation, intellectual disability, autism and epilepsy (Keppler-Noreuil et al., 2014; Mirzaa et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: FCD represents one of the most common causes of intractable epilepsy.
source: FCD represents one of the most common causes of intractable epilepsy (Bast et al., 2006; Fauser et al., 2015; Fauser, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Conditional mouse alleles for the H1047R and E545K Pik3ca hotspot mutations have been generated to study tumor formation and assess anti-cancer activities of pathway inhibitors.
source: Conditional mouse alleles for the H1047R and E545K Pik3ca hotspot mutations have been generated to study tumor formation and assess anti-cancer activities of pathway inhibitors (Kinross et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2011; Meyer et al., 2011; Robinson et al., 2012; Yuan et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature describing these mouse models.

claim: The severity of brain phenotypes critically depended on the Pik3ca allele and its time of activation.
source: The severity of these brain phenotypes critically depended on the Pik3ca allele and its time of activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing different alleles and activation times.

claim: Pik3ca-associated epilepsy in mice was independent of brain overgrowth and cortical dysplasia.
source: Notably, Pik3ca-associated epilepsy in mice was independent of brain overgrowth and cortical dysplasia.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing epilepsy in normocephalic Nestin-creER;E545K mice.

claim: Seizures of adult megalencephalic mice were suppressed by acute 1 hr-administration of pan-PI3K inhibitor BKM120.
source: Further the seizures of adult megalencephalic mice were suppressed by acute 1 hr-administration of pan-PI3K inhibitor BKM120 (Maira et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 7 showing BKM120 effects on seizures.

claim: Epilepsy in Pik3ca mouse models represents an active Pik3ca-driven process that can be restricted by dynamic modulation of PI3K pathway activity in dysmorphic brains.
source: We conclude that epilepsy in these models represents an active Pik3ca-driven process that can be restricted by dynamic modulation of PI3K pathway activity in dysmorphic brains.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the BKM120 treatment data.

claim: All hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants exhibited progressive hydrocephalus and died prior to weaning when doxycycline was administered from embryonic day (E)0.5.
source: The most severe phenotype was achieved in hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants, when doxycycline was administered from embryonic day (E)0.5. All mutants exhibited progressive hydrocephalus and died prior to weaning.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations of the H1047R mutant phenotype.

claim: Hydrocephalus was evident as a domed forehead at postnatal day (P)21 in hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants.
source: Hydrocephalus was evident as a domed forehead at postnatal day (P)21 (Figure 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by visual evidence in Figure 1b.

claim: Hematoxylin-eosin stained P3 sections showed ventriculomegaly in the megalencephalic H1047R mutant brains.
source: Hematoxylin-eosin stained P3 sections showed ventriculomegaly in the megalencephalic H1047R mutant brains.
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1c,d.

claim: The hippocampus was not evident in H1047R mutants, and instead the medial tissue was highly dysplastic with multiple infoldings along its entire length.
source: Strikingly the hippocampus was not evident in these mutants. Instead, the medial tissue was highly dysplastic with multiple infoldings along its entire length (Figure 1c,d).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 1c,d.

claim: When pups were treated with doxycycline from P1, no morphological differences were observed between the control and the hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutant.
source: In contrast, when pups were treated with doxycycline from P1, no morphological differences were observed between the control and the hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutant (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The effect of H1047R mutation on brain size was dependent on time of activation.
source: Thus the effect of H1047R mutation on brain size was dependent on time of activation.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the comparison of embryonic vs postnatal doxycycline administration.

claim: P35 hGFAP-cre;E545K and Nestin-cre;E545K brains were noticeably larger than controls.
source: P35 hGFAP-cre;E545K and Nestin-cre;E545K brains were noticeably larger than controls, while Nestin-creER;E545K mutants had normal-sized brains compared to controls.
evidence: This claim is supported by visual and volumetric data in Figure 1e-h.

claim: Nestin-creER;E545K mutants had normal-sized brains compared to controls.
source: P35 hGFAP-cre;E545K and Nestin-cre;E545K brains were noticeably larger than controls, while Nestin-creER;E545K mutants had normal-sized brains compared to controls.
evidence: This claim is supported by volumetric data in Figure 1g,h.

claim: hGFAP-cre;E545K mice had a milder phenotype than hGFAP-cre;H1047R mice, surviving as adults without hydrocephalus, though their brain size was significantly larger compared to control littermates.
source: E545K mice with the same cre-driver (hGFAP-cre;E545K) had a milder phenotype, surviving as adults without hydrocephalus, though their brain size was significantly larger compared to control littermates (Figure 1e,h,j).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing E545K and H1047R phenotypes.

claim: With identical time of activation by the same cre driver, the brain phenotypes are dependent on specific Pik3ca allele.
source: This provides evidence that with identical time of activation by the same cre driver, the brain phenotypes are dependent on specific Pik3ca allele.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from comparing hGFAP-cre;H1047R and hGFAP-cre;E545K phenotypes.

claim: Earlier activation of E545K mutation with Nestin-cre led to a 54.4% volumetric increase, with mild ventriculomegaly and no hydrocephalus.
source: Earlier activation of E545K mutation with Nestin-cre led to an even more striking 54.4% volumetric increase, with mild ventriculomegaly and no hydrocephalus (Figure 1f,h,k).
evidence: This claim is supported by volumetric MRI data in Figure 1h.

claim: Neonatal activation of E545K using Nestin-creER had no apparent impact on brain size.
source: Interestingly, neonatal activation of E545K using Nestin-creER had no apparent impact on brain size (Figure 1g,h,l).
evidence: This claim is supported by volumetric data in Figure 1h.

claim: Enlarged head size in both Nestin-cre;E545K and hGFAP-cre;E545K mutants was evident at birth and brain size of all the three adult E545K mutants was relatively stable.
source: Enlarged head size in both Nestin-cre;E545K and hGFAP-cre;E545K mutants was evident at birth and brain size of all the three adult E545K mutants was relatively stable (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is based on experimental observations not shown in figures.

claim: Gross morphology was normal for all E545K mutants.
source: Unlike H1047R mutants, gross morphology was normal for all E545K mutants.
evidence: This claim is supported by visual inspection of brain sections in Figure 1.

claim: To cause brain overgrowth, overactivation of Pik3ca function is required during embryogenesis.
source: Further, we conclude that to cause brain overgrowth, overactivation of Pik3ca function is required during embryogenesis.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the timing experiments showing no overgrowth with postnatal activation.

claim: The inner cortical length of hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants was longer than controls at both E14.5 and E16.5.
source: The inner cortical length of hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants was longer than controls at both E14.5 (p<0.01) and E16.5 (p<0.001; Figure 2b–g).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 2.

claim: hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants showed enlarged nuclear and cell size at both E14.5 and E16.5.
source: This was accompanied by enlarged nuclear and cell size at both ages and decreased cell density at E16.5, but not increased proliferation or cell cycle exit (Figure 3c–l).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3.

claim: hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants showed decreased cell density at E16.5.
source: This was accompanied by enlarged nuclear and cell size at both ages and decreased cell density at E16.5, but not increased proliferation or cell cycle exit (Figure 3c–l).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3.

claim: hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants did not show increased proliferation or cell cycle exit.
source: This was accompanied by enlarged nuclear and cell size at both ages and decreased cell density at E16.5, but not increased proliferation or cell cycle exit (Figure 3c–l).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3.

claim: Total cell number per cortical column length was not significantly different between control and H1047R mutant both at E14.5 and E16.5.
source: Total cell number per cortical column length was not significantly different between control and H1047R mutant both at E14.5 and E16.5.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: TUNEL+ cell number was significantly lower in E16.5 H1047R mutant cortex than in control.
source: Also, TUNEL+ cell number was significantly lower in E16.5 mutant cortex than in control (p<0.01), indicating reduced apoptosis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1a,c); however the overall TUNEL+ cell numbers for both control and mutant were small.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative TUNEL data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cortical expansion in hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutant was not primarily driven by increased proliferation or reduced apoptosis; rather reduced cell density and increased cell size during embryogenesis were major contributing factors.
source: Together these results indicate that cortical expansion in hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutant was not primarily driven by increased proliferation or reduced apoptosis; rather reduced cell density and increased cell size during embryogenesis were major contributing factors.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the combined developmental data.

claim: In Nestin-cre;E545K mutants, the inner cortical length was comparable to controls at E14.5 but elongated at E16.5.
source: By contrast, in Nestin-cre;E545K mutants, the inner cortical length was comparable to controls at E14.5 but elongated at E16.5 (p<0.01); cortical thickness was slightly reduced in E16.5 (p<0.05) as compared to controls (Figure 2h–m).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements in Figure 2.

claim: Cortical thickness was slightly reduced in E16.5 Nestin-cre;E545K mutants as compared to controls.
source: By contrast, in Nestin-cre;E545K mutants, the inner cortical length was comparable to controls at E14.5 but elongated at E16.5 (p<0.01); cortical thickness was slightly reduced in E16.5 (p<0.05) as compared to controls (Figure 2h–m).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements in Figure 2.

claim: The labeling index was similar to the control at E14.5 but increased in E16.5 Nestin-cre;E545K mutants, indicating more proliferation.
source: The labeling index was similar to the control at E14.5 but increased in E16.5 mutants (p<0.05), indicating more proliferation (Figure 3m,o,r).
evidence: This claim is supported by BrdU labeling data in Figure 3.

claim: Cell density in E545K mutant neocortex was similar to the control at E14.5 but was reduced at E16.5.
source: Cell density in E545K mutant neocortex was similar to the control at E14.5 but was reduced at E16.5 (p<0.05).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3.

claim: Total cells per cortical column length did not change in the E545K mutant.
source: Total cells per cortical column length did not change in the E545K mutant; but the TUNEL+ cell number was lower in E16.5 mutant cortex than in control (p<0.001).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: TUNEL+ cell number was lower in E16.5 E545K mutant cortex than in control.
source: Total cells per cortical column length did not change in the E545K mutant; but the TUNEL+ cell number was lower in E16.5 mutant cortex than in control (p<0.001).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative TUNEL data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The nuclear size of E545K mutant cells was similar to controls at both E14.5 and E16.5 but cell somas were significantly larger at E16.5.
source: Intriguingly, the nuclear size of these mutant cells was similar to controls at both E14.5 and E16.5 but cell somas were significantly larger (p<0.05) at E16.5 (Figure 3n,p,q,s,t).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements in Figure 3.

claim: The quit fraction indicative of rate of cells exiting cell cycle was significantly higher in the E545K mutant between E15.5 and E16.5.
source: The quit fraction indicative of rate of cells exiting cell cycle was significantly higher (p<0.05) in the E545K mutant between E15.5 and E16.5 (Figure 3u,v).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell cycle exit data in Figure 3.

claim: At P35, the neocortical cells of Nestin-cre;E545K mutant were larger compared to controls.
source: At P35, the neocortical cells of Nestin-cre;E545K mutant were still larger (p<0.05) compared to controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a,b).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: In the adult P35 Nestin-creER;E545K mutant mice, where activation was initiated in neonates and brain size was not different from controls, E545K-activated (YFP+) cells have the same size as controls.
source: Notably, in the adult P35 Nestin-creER;E545K mutant mice, where activation was initiated in neonates, and brain size was not different from controls, E545K-activated (YFP+) cells have the same size as controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 2c,d).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Increased cell size due to E545K overactivation has a critical embryonic period.
source: We conclude that increased cell size due to E545K overactivation also has a critical embryonic period.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the timing experiments showing no cell size increase with postnatal activation.

claim: Changes in multiple developmental parameters including proliferation, cell cycle exit, cell size and density contribute to MEG of Nestin-cre;E545K Pik3ca embryonic overactivation.
source: Further, changes in multiple developmental parameters including proliferation, cell cycle exit, cell size and density contribute to MEG of Nestin-cre;E545K Pik3ca embryonic overactivation.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the combined developmental data for E545K mutants.

claim: Disordered lamination is a key feature of human SEGCD.
source: Since disordered lamination is a key feature of human SEGCD (Arai et al., 2012; Rossini et al., 2014), we assessed neocortical organization and development in both hGFAP-cre;H1047R and Nestin-cre;E545K mutants.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on human SEGCD pathology.

claim: In H1047R mutants, the radial glial scaffold was slightly fasciculated and irregular at E14.5 and E16.5.
source: In H1047R mutants, the radial glial scaffold was slightly fasciculated and irregular at E14.5 and E16.5.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Irregularities in radial glial scaffold were very prominent at P0 in H1047R mutants when a disrupted pial surface was associated with irregular clusters of enlarged radial glial end-feet.
source: Irregularities were very prominent at P0 when a disrupted pial surface was associated with irregular clusters of enlarged radial glial end-feet (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The radial glial phenotype was much more subtle in the E545K mutant at E14.5 and E16.5.
source: The radial glial phenotype was much more subtle in the E545K mutant at E14.5 and E16.5; however at P0, we observed thinning of radial glial fibers and irregular clusters of end-feet at the intact pial surface (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: At P0, E545K mutants showed thinning of radial glial fibers and irregular clusters of end-feet at the intact pial surface.
source: The radial glial phenotype was much more subtle in the E545K mutant at E14.5 and E16.5; however at P0, we observed thinning of radial glial fibers and irregular clusters of end-feet at the intact pial surface (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Cajal-Retzius cells expressing Reelin were normally present in an ordered array in the marginal zone (layer I) of controls and Nestin-cre;E545K mice.
source: Cajal-Retzius cells expressing Reelin, a major regulator of radial migration, were normally present in an ordered array in the marginal zone (layer I) of controls and Nestin-cre;E545K mice (Figure 4b; Figure 5b,c).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Cajal-Retzius cells were dysplastic in hGFAP-cre;H1047R mice at E16.5.
source: However, these cells were dysplastic in hGFAP-cre;H1047R mice at E16.5 (Figure 4c,c').
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 4.

claim: Ectopic Reelin-positive cells were not observed within the cortical column in either mutant.
source: We did not observe ectopic Reelin-positive cells within the cortical column in either mutant.
evidence: This claim is based on observation of immunohistochemical data.

claim: hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants displayed a marked disorganization of all layers with Ctip2/Tbr1-positive as well as Cux1-positive cells dispersed throughout the cortical plate.
source: hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants displayed a marked disorganization of all layers. Ctip2/Tbr1-positive as well as Cux1-positive cells in the E16.5 H1047R mutant were dispersed throughout the cortical plate, with both early- and late-born neurons severely mislocalized (Figure 4d–g).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 4.

claim: Laminar disorganization was less severe in E16.5 Nestin-cre;E545K brains, but deep Ctip2/Tbr1-positive neurons and upper Cux1-positive neurons were dispersed throughout the cortical plate.
source: Laminar disorganization was less severe in E16.5 Nestin-cre;E545K brains, but deep Ctip2/Tbr1-positive neurons and upper Cux1-positive neurons were dispersed throughout the cortical plate (Figure 5f,g).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 5.

claim: Laminar patterns in postnatal animals remained disrupted in both mutants, with hGFAP-cre;H1047R cortex more affected than Nestin-cre;E545K mutant cortex.
source: Laminar patterns in postnatal animals remained disrupted in both mutants, with hGFAP-cre;H1047R cortex more affected Nestin-cre;E545K mutant cortex (Figure 5h–m).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: A simple developmental delay was not the cause of dysplasia.
source: Thus a simple developmental delay was not the cause of dysplasia (Figure 4h–m; Figure 5h–m).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the persistence of dysplasia in postnatal animals.

claim: In P3 hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants, NeuN-positive mature cortical neurons were found within the normally cell-sparse marginal zone as well as in the cortical white matter and residual ventricular zone.
source: In P3 hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants, NeuN-positive mature cortical neurons were found within the normally cell-sparse marginal zone as well as in the cortical white matter and residual ventricular zone, a feature reported in SEGCD patients (Arai et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 4 and comparison to human pathology.

claim: The cortical subplate was not readily discernible in P3 hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants, blurring the boundary between grey and white matter.
source: Further, the cortical subplate was not readily discernible in these mutants (Figure 4h–k; Figure 4—figure supplement 2e,f), blurring the boundary between grey and white matter – a feature often observed in SEGCD patients (Rossini et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data in Figure 4 and comparison to human pathology.

claim: The total numbers of BrdU+ P0 cells, born at E12.5 and E16.5, were not significantly different between controls and either hGFAP-cre;H1047R or Nestin-cre;E545K mutants.
source: The total numbers of BrdU+ P0 cells, born at E12.5 and E16.5, were not significantly different between controls and either hGFAP-cre;H1047R or Nestin-cre;E545K mutants (Figure 6b,j).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative birthdating data in Figure 6.

claim: The distribution of BrdU+ cells showed significant differences between controls and H1047R mutants labelled during both early and late embryonic stages.
source: The distribution of BrdU+ cells showed significant differences between controls and H1047R mutants labelled during both early and late embryonic stages. At P0, more BrdU+ cells were localized in the lower cortical plate (CP) and white matter (Figure 6c).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative birthdating data in Figure 6.

claim: For E545K mutants the BrdU+ cell numbers were not different at either age, but the distribution was subtly yet significantly different only for the early born neurons.
source: For E545K mutants the BrdU+ cell numbers were not different at either age. The distribution was subtly, yet significantly different only for the early born neurons (Figure 6k).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative birthdating data in Figure 6.

claim: For both the H1047R and E545K Pik3ca activating alleles, total layer V (Ctip2+) cell numbers at P0 were not significantly different between controls and mutants.
source: For both the H1047R and E545K Pik3ca activating alleles, total layer V (Ctip2+) cell numbers at P0 were not significantly different between controls and mutants (Figure 6d,l).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 6.

claim: The numbers of Ctip2/BrdU double-labeled cells were the same in controls and mutants, indicating that cell fate specification for these deep layer neurons was unaffected by either the H1047R or E545K Pik3ca allele.
source: Also, the numbers of Ctip2/BrdU double-labeled cells were the same in controls and mutants, indicating that cell fate specification for these deep layer neurons was unaffected by either the H1047R or E545K Pik3ca allele (Figure 6e,m).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the birthdating data showing normal numbers of fate-specified neurons.

claim: The specific distribution of layer V neurons was abnormal in H1047R mutants, with ectopic Ctip2/BrdU double-labeled cells in the upper and lower CP and white matter, instead of mid CP.
source: However, similar to the overall BrdU+ cell distribution, the specific distribution of layer V neurons was abnormal in H1047R mutants, with ectopic Ctip2/BrdU double-labeled cells in the upper and lower CP and white matter, instead of mid CP (Figure 6f).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative birthdating data in Figure 6.

claim: In E545K mutants, fewer Ctip2+ cells were positioned in the mid CP, although the phenotype was much less severe than H1047R.
source: In E545K mutants, fewer Ctip2+ cells were positioned in the mid CP (Figure 6n), although the phenotype was much less severe.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 6.

claim: Upper layer (Cux1+) neuronal numbers and distributions were significantly different in both H1047R and E545K mutants, compared to their respective controls.
source: Upper layer (Cux1+) neuronal numbers and distributions were significantly different in both H1047R and E545K mutants, compared to their respective controls (Figure 6g,o).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data in Figure 6.

claim: In E545K mutants, the increase in total Cux1+ cell numbers corresponded to increased Cux1/BrdU double-labeled cells, born at E16.5.
source: In E545K mutants, the increase in total Cux1+ cell numbers in the E545K mutant corresponded to increased Cux1/BrdU double-labeled cells, born at E16.5 (Figure 6p).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative birthdating data in Figure 6.

claim: No correlation was observed between Cux1+ cell numbers and Cux1/BrdU double-labeled cells in E12.5 or E16.5-born cells in the H1047R mutant.
source: However, no such correlation was observed in E12.5 or E16.5-born Cux1+ cells in the H1047R mutant (Figure 6h).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative birthdating data in Figure 6.

claim: Extra Cux1+ cells in H1047R mutants were likely born between E16.5 and P0.
source: These extra cells were therefore likely born between E16.5 and P0.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the birthdating data.

claim: Cell fates are largely correctly specified in both Pik3ca mutants and cortical dysplasia is more likely caused by aberrant neuronal migration.
source: Together, these data indicate that cell fates are largely correctly specified in both Pik3ca mutants and that cortical dysplasia is more likely caused by aberrant neuronal migration.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the combined birthdating and lamination data.

claim: In P3 hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants, the underlying cortical white matter was much thicker than controls, although the cortical plate itself was not dramatically thicker.
source: In P3 hGFAP-cre;H1047R mutants, although the cortical plate itself was not dramatically thicker than controls, the underlying cortical white matter was much thicker (Figure 4j,k; Figure 4—figure suplement 2e,f).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data in Figure 4.

claim: White matter thickening was less pronounced but readily discernible in P3 Nestin-cre;E545K mutants.
source: This was less pronounced but readily discernible in P3 Nestin-cre;E545K mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 2c,d).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: In P3 H1047R mutants, there was complete absence of corpus callosum, although hippocampal and anterior commissures were present.
source: In P3 H1047R mutants, there was complete absence of corpus callosum, although hippocampal and anterior commissures were present (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a-d).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: All major tracts were present in P3 E545K mutants.
source: In contrast, all major tracts were present in P3 E545K mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The white matter phenotypes are consistent with the wide spectrum of white matter dysplasia reported in MEG and SEGCD patients.
source: These data are consistent with the wide spectrum of white matter dysplasia reported in MEG and SEGCD patients (Conway et al., 2007; Adamsbaum et al., 1998; De Rosa et al., 1992; Jansen et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is based on comparison to human pathology cited in the literature.

claim: Increased number of Olig2-positive cells was observed in the white matter area of both H1047R and E545K mutants.
source: Moreover, increased number of Olig2-positive cells was observed in the white matter area of both H1047R and E545K mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in the figure supplements.

claim: Astrocytosis is not a feature of PIK3CA-pathology in the mouse models.
source: Although astrocytosis is observed when mTOR signaling is activated by TSC mutations in humans and mice (Sosunov et al., 2008; Zeng et al., 2008), it is not a feature of PIK3CA-pathology in our mouse models (Figure 5—figure supplement 3a-d).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Epilepsy is one of the most important clinical features of SEGCD.
source: Epilepsy is one of the most important clinical features of SEGCD (Bast et al., 2006; Fauser et al., 2015; Fauser, 2006; Arai et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on SEGCD.

claim: Baseline sleep EEG recordings in both Nestin-cre;E545K and Nestin-creER;E545K animal models revealed epileptiform activity including sets of spikes/polyspikes, and regional and generalized spike and wave discharges during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep.
source: Baseline sleep EEG recordings in both animal models revealed epileptiform activity including sets of spikes/polyspikes, and regional and generalized spike and wave discharges during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep (Figure 7b,c).
evidence: This claim is supported by EEG data in Figure 7.

claim: The frequency of epileptiform interictal activity was increased in post sleep deprivation EEG recordings in Nestin-creER;E545K mice.
source: The frequency of epileptiform interictal activity was increased in post sleep deprivation EEG recordings, and clinically relevant spontaneous seizures including myoclonic (MC) seizures, frequent isolated spikes, and train of spikes, were observed in the Nestin-creER;E545K mice (Figure 7d,e).
evidence: This claim is supported by EEG data in Figure 7.

claim: Clinically relevant spontaneous seizures including myoclonic (MC) seizures, frequent isolated spikes, and train of spikes, were observed in the Nestin-creER;E545K mice after sleep deprivation.
source: The frequency of epileptiform interictal activity was increased in post sleep deprivation EEG recordings, and clinically relevant spontaneous seizures including myoclonic (MC) seizures, frequent isolated spikes, and train of spikes, were observed in the Nestin-creER;E545K mice (Figure 7d,e).
evidence: This claim is supported by EEG data in Figure 7.

claim: Both the megalencephalic and normocephalic E545K mouse models exhibited lower seizure thresholds compared to controls at both P35 and P180 when challenged with PTZ.
source: When challenged with the chemoconvulsant pentylenetetrazol (PTZ), a GABA-A receptor antagonist (Macdonald and Barker, 1978), both the megalencephalic and normocephalic E545K mouse models exhibited lower seizure thresholds compared to controls at both P35 and P180 (Figure 7f–i; Figure 7—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This claim is supported by PTZ seizure induction data in Figure 7.

claim: In the 30 min post PTZ injection, both E545K models showed shorter latencies to first generalized tonic clonic (GTC) seizures, more myoclonic seizures, and a prolonged seizure load.
source: In the 30 min post PTZ injection, both models showed shorter latencies to first generalized tonic clonic (GTC) seizures, more myoclonic seizures, and a prolonged seizure load.
evidence: This claim is supported by PTZ seizure data in Figure 7 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Pik3ca overactivation is sufficient to cause epilepsy.
source: We conclude that Pik3ca overactivation is sufficient to cause epilepsy.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the epilepsy phenotypes observed in the mouse models.

claim: Pik3ca-related epilepsy is dissociable from brain overgrowth and cortical dysplasia.
source: Further our data indicate that Pik3ca-related epilepsy is dissociable from brain overgrowth and cortical dysplasia.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the observation that normocephalic Nestin-creER;E545K mice also have epilepsy.

claim: BKM120 is an orally available pan-Class I PI3K inhibitor currently in clinical trials for solid tumors.
source: BKM120, a 2,6-dimorpholino pyrimidine derivative, is an orally available pan-Class I PI3K inhibitor currently in clinical trials for solid tumors (Maira et al., 2012; Bendell et al., 2012; Brachmann et al., 2012) and may represent a novel therapeutic agent for PIK3CA-related epilepsy.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on BKM120.

claim: Preclinical studies show that BKM120 maximally inhibits downstream phosphorylation of Akt, 1hr post-administration.
source: Preclinical studies show that BKM120 maximally inhibits downstream phosphorylation of Akt, 1hr post-administration (Maira et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature on BKM120 pharmacodynamics.

claim: BKM120 increased the seizure threshold of control animals.
source: BKM120 increased the seizure threshold of control animals.
evidence: This claim is supported by PTZ seizure data in Figure 7.

claim: Despite the presence of megalencephaly and considerable cortical dysplasia in P35 Nestin-cre;E545K megencephalic animals, BKM120 dramatically decreased the seizure number and duration to untreated control levels and marginally increased seizure latency in the mutant mice.
source: More importantly, despite the presence of megalencephaly and considerable cortical dysplasia in P35 Nestin-cre;E545K megencephalic animals, BKM120 dramatically decreased the seizure number and duration to untreated control levels and marginally increased seizure latency in the mutant mice (Figure 7h,i; Figure 7—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: This claim is supported by BKM120 treatment data in Figure 7.

claim: Dynamic Pik3ca-dependent processes, independent of cortical and cellular dysplasia, cause Pik3ca-related epilepsy and they are highly amenable to therapeutic intervention.
source: These data powerfully demonstrate that dynamic Pik3ca-dependent processes, independent of cortical and cellular dysplasia, cause Pik3ca-related epilepsy and they are highly amenable to therapeutic intervention.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the BKM120 treatment results.

claim: Untreated Nestin-cre;E545K mutants exhibited significant elevations of phospho (p)S473-Akt and pT346-NDRG1, consistent with PI3K pathway activation.
source: As expected, untreated Nestin-cre;E545K mutants exhibited significant elevations of phospho (p)S473-Akt and pT346-NDRG1, consistent with PI3K pathway activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RPPA data in Figure 8.

claim: Baseline pS473-Akt levels in the Nestin-cre;E545K hippocampus were prominently higher than the cortical levels.
source: Notably, baseline pS473-Akt levels in the Nestin-cre;E545K hippocampus were prominently higher than the cortical levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by RPPA data in Figure 8.

claim: In both E545K mutant and control brain tissues, PTZ treatment alone increased the levels of pAkt, especially pS473-Akt, of pS6 (pS235/S236, pS240/244), pT346-NDRG1 and pS2448-mTOR.
source: In both E545K mutant and control brain tissues, PTZ treatment alone increased the levels of pAkt, especially pS473-Akt, of pS6 (pS235/S236, pS240/244), pT346-NDRG1 and pS2448-mTOR.
evidence: This claim is supported by RPPA data in Figure 8.

claim: Acute BKM120 treatment alone reduced phosphorylation of multiple PI3K pathway members, including AKT, S6, NDRG1, GSK3 and 4EBP1.
source: As expected, acute BKM120 treatment alone reduced phosphorylation of multiple PI3K pathway members, including AKT, S6, NDRG1, GSK3 and 4EBP1.
evidence: This claim is supported by RPPA data in Figure 8.

claim: BKM120 inhibited the increased phosphorylation levels induced by PTZ, notably returning mutant hippocampal pS473-AKT levels to baseline untreated control levels.
source: Most remarkably, BKM120 also inhibited the increased phosphorylation levels induced by PTZ, notably returning mutant hippocampal pS473-AKT levels to baseline untreated control levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by RPPA data in Figure 8.

claim: E545K mutation accounts for 26% and H1047R for 38% of PIK3CA-coding mutations detected in the COSMIC database of cancer mutations.
source: For example, E545K mutation accounts for 1932/7548 (26%) and H1047R for 2898/7548 (38%) of PIK3CA-coding mutations detected in the COSMIC database of cancer mutations (http://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/cancergenome/projects/cosmic).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from the COSMIC database.

claim: H1047R mutation is more severe than E545K mutation in mice.
source: We found that H1047R and E545K mutations caused distinct phenotypes in mice, H1047R being more severe than E545K.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of phenotypes across the manuscript.

claim: The phenotypic differences between H1047R and E545K more likely reflect distinct allele-specific overactivation of PI3K signaling rather than differences in expression levels.
source: We do not believe that overexpression of the transgenic H1047R allele versus the knock-in design of the E545K allele underlies the phenotypic differences. The PI3K enzyme is made of p110 (encoded by Pik3ca) and p85 subunits. p110 stability is entirely dependent on levels of p85 (Geering et al., 2007; Fruman et al., 2000; Yu et al., 1998) and we have not altered p85. Rather, the phenotypic differences more likely reflect distinct allele-specific overactivation of PI3K signaling.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from knowledge of PI3K enzyme structure and function.

claim: The H1047R mutation increases the level and duration of response to extracellular ligand, while E545K alters the helical domain resulting in constitutive low level signaling with a blunted response to extracellular ligands.
source: The H1047R mutation increases the level and duration of response to extracellular ligand, while E545K alters the helical domain resulting in constitutive low level signaling with a blunted response to extracellular ligands (Miled et al., 2007; Zhao and Vogt, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on the biochemical properties of these mutations.

claim: By activating the E545K mutation in progressively limited progenitor pools, brain and cell size decreased in a graduated fashion.
source: By activating the E545K mutation in progressively limited progenitor pools, we decreased the size of brain and cells in a graduated fashion.
evidence: This claim is supported by data comparing different cre drivers in Figure 1.

claim: Postnatal E545K activation had no impact on cell/brain size.
source: Postnatal E545K activation had no impact on cell/brain size.
evidence: This claim is supported by data on Nestin-creER;E545K mice in Figures 1 and 3.

claim: PIK3CA-related brain overgrowth must arise from mosaic mutations in embryonic neural progenitors.
source: We conclude that the PIK3CA-related brain overgrowth must arise from mosaic mutations in embryonic neural progenitors.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the timing experiments.

claim: Neuronal size was enlarged in both hGFAP-cre;H1047R and Nestin-cre;E545K mutants, but it was less than that observed in Pten null mice or in cultured hippocampal neurons constitutively overexpressing Akt.
source: Although neuronal size was enlarged in both hGFAP-cre;H1047R and Nestin-cre;E545K mutants, it was less than that observed in Pten null mice or in cultured hippocampal neurons constitutively overexpressing Akt (Kumar, 2005; Kwon et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is based on comparison to prior literature on Pten and Akt models.

claim: Multiple models of Pten deletion cause progressive increases in postnatal neuronal size and increased brain size without continued proliferation.
source: Multiple models of Pten deletion cause progressive increases in postnatal neuronal size and increased brain size without continued proliferation (Kwon et al., 2001; Fraser, 2004; Fraser et al., 2008; Backman et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on Pten models.

claim: Nestin-cre;E545K mutants had enlarged brain size evident at birth, without progressive increases in postnatal cell size.
source: Our Nestin-cre;E545K mutants had enlarged brain size evident at birth, without progressive increases in postnatal cell size.
evidence: This claim is supported by developmental data in the manuscript.

claim: Mild cellular enlargement was observed with PIK3CA mutations in contrast to marked enlargement with PTEN or AKT3 mutations in resected human brain tissue from SEGCD patients.
source: This is congruent with the analysis of resected human brain tissue from SEGCD patients. Mild cellular enlargement was observed with PIK3CA mutations in contrast to marked enlargement with PTEN or AKT3 mutations (Jansen et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature on human SEGCD pathology.

claim: Brains of SEGCD patients show mild to moderate migration defects in early-born cortical neurons and more severe defects in late-born neurons.
source: Brains of SEGCD patients show mild to moderate migration defects in early-born cortical neurons and more severe defects in late-born neurons (Arai et al., 2012; Rossini et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on human SEGCD pathology.

claim: Embryonic activation of H1047R and E545K in mice caused abnormal neocortical lamination, with late-migrating Cux1-positive neurons severely affected in both the mutants.
source: Similarly, embryonic activation of H1047R and E545K in mice caused abnormal neocortical lamination, with late-migrating Cux1-positive neurons severely affected in both the mutants.
evidence: This claim is supported by lamination data in Figures 4-6.

claim: Birthdating studies support the conclusion that Pik3ca activation does not alter cell fate and that cortical dysplasia is predominantly a result of aberrant migration.
source: Birthdating studies support the conclusion that Pik3ca activation does not alter cell fate and that cortical dysplasia is predominantly a result of aberrant migration.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the birthdating data in Figure 6.

claim: The severity of dyslamination in H1047R mutants likely reflects the dysplastic Reelin-positive Cajal-Retzius cells.
source: The severity of dyslamination in H1047R mutants likely reflects the dysplastic Reelin-positive Cajal-Retzius cells.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the Reelin staining data in Figure 4.

claim: In human SEGCD, late migrating neurons often fail to migrate to the upper layers, a phenotype more severe than seen in any of the mouse models.
source: In human SEGCD, late migrating neurons often fail to migrate to the upper layers (Arai et al., 2012), a phenotype more severe than seen in any of our mouse models.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison to human pathology cited in the literature.

claim: NeuN immunohistochemistry in H1047R mutants confirmed the presence of ectopic neurons in the subcortical white matter, as seen in human SEGCD brain.
source: However, NeuN immunohistochemistry in H1047R mutants confirmed the presence of ectopic neurons in the subcortical white matter, as seen in human SEGCD brain (Arai et al., 2012; Salamon, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemical data and comparison to human pathology.

claim: Human MEG is associated with a wide range of white matter dysplasia ranging from agenesis of corpus callosum to thickening of subcortical axon bundles.
source: Human MEG is associated with a wide range of white matter dysplasia ranging from agenesis of corpus callosum to thickening of subcortical axon bundles (Conway et al., 2007; Adamsbaum et al., 1998; De Rosa et al., 1992; Jansen et al., 2015; Salamon, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on human MEG pathology.

claim: White matter dysplasia features were faithfully recapitulated in the mouse models.
source: These features were also faithfully recapitulated in our mouse models.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of mouse data to human pathology.

claim: Cortical dysplasia resulted from embryonic activation of Pik3ca in Nestin-cre;E545K mice.
source: Although cortical dysplasia resulted from embryonic activation of Pik3ca in Nestin-cre;E545K mice, postnatal activation of Nestin-creER;E545K did not cause increased cell size or megalencephaly or altered cortical lamination.
evidence: This claim is supported by lamination data in Figure 5.

claim: Postnatal activation of Nestin-creER;E545K did not cause increased cell size or megalencephaly or altered cortical lamination.
source: Although cortical dysplasia resulted from embryonic activation of Pik3ca in Nestin-cre;E545K mice, postnatal activation of Nestin-creER;E545K did not cause increased cell size or megalencephaly or altered cortical lamination.
evidence: This claim is supported by data on Nestin-creER;E545K mice in Figures 1 and 3.

claim: Inhibitory interneurons were not grossly perturbed in Nestin-creER;E545K mice.
source: Further, inhibitory interneurons were not grossly perturbed in Nestin-creER;E545K mice (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is based on experimental observations not shown in figures.

claim: Interneurons are born at embryonic stages and their migration is almost complete before birth.
source: This is congruent with the fact that these interneurons are born at embryonic stages and their migration is almost complete before birth (Batista‐Brito and Fishell, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature on interneuron development.

claim: Altered interneuron development in Nestin-cre;E545K may contribute to epilepsy, but aberrant interneuron development cannot represent a common mechanism for epilepsy in both models.
source: Therefore altered interneuron development in Nestin-cre;E545K may contribute to epilepsy, aberrant interneuron development cannot represent a common mechanism for epilepsy in both models.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the interneuron data and comparison between models.

claim: The observation that acute BKM120 treatment is sufficient to inhibit PTZ-induced seizures even in adult megalencephalic mice supports the argument that the epileptic seizures are independent of dysplasia.
source: The observation that acute BKM120 treatment is sufficient to inhibit PTZ-induced seizures even in adult megalencephalic mice supports the argument that the epileptic seizures are independent of dysplasia since the latter is not reversed over the short course of treatment.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the BKM120 treatment data.

claim: A large portion of FCD patients who do not show detectable dysplasia suffer from intractable epilepsy.
source: This is an important finding since a large portion of FCD patients who do not show detectable dysplasia suffer from intractable epilepsy (Bernasconi et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature on FCD.

claim: Nestin-cre;E545K mutants had elevated PI3K signaling with a more robust upregulation of mTOR-dependent pS473-Akt than the direct PDK1-dependent pT308-Akt.
source: Nestin-cre;E545K mutants had elevated PI3K signaling with a more robust upregulation of mTOR-dependent pS473-Akt than the direct PDK1-dependent pT308-Akt, similar to the recent findings in human brain samples with PIK3CA mutations (Jansen et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by RPPA data in Figure 8 and comparison to human data.

claim: The modest changes in signaling compared to controls is congruent with previous studies which demonstrated only modest changes in the steady-state levels of PI3K signaling in breast cancer cells with PIK3CA mutations.
source: The modest changes in signaling compared to controls is congruent with previous studies which demonstrated only modest changes in the steady-state levels of PI3K signaling in breast cancer cells with PIK3CA mutations (Stemke-Hale et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is based on comparison to prior literature on PIK3CA signaling in cancer.

claim: Higher signaling levels in hippocampus versus cortex suggest a more prominent role of hippocampus in the seizure phenotype.
source: Higher signaling levels in hippocampus versus cortex suggest a more prominent role of hippocampus in the seizure phenotype.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the RPPA data showing regional differences.

claim: PTZ-induced seizures in rats upregulated PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway.
source: This is congruent with a report showing PTZ-induced seizures in rats upregulated PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway (Zhang and Wong, 2012) and suggests that elevated baseline PI3K signaling levels are epileptogenic.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature on PTZ effects.

claim: Elevated baseline PI3K signaling levels are epileptogenic.
source: This is congruent with a report showing PTZ-induced seizures in rats upregulated PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway (Zhang and Wong, 2012) and suggests that elevated baseline PI3K signaling levels are epileptogenic.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the RPPA data and comparison to prior literature.

claim: There is extensive human and mouse evidence that elevated mTOR signaling is epileptogenic.
source: Indeed, there is extensive human and mouse evidence that elevated mTOR signaling is epileptogenic although the mechanisms for the epilepsy are incompletely understood.
evidence: This claim is supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: Mechanisms for mTOR-related epilepsy include altered development, cell size, growth, proliferation and circuitry.
source: A number of mechanisms including altered development, cell size, growth, proliferation and circuitry have been reported (Wong and Crino, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature on mTOR-related epilepsy mechanisms.

claim: Acute BKM120 administration data clearly demonstrates that histopathological mechanisms are not the primary epilepsy drivers.
source: Most remarkably however, our acute BKM120 administration data clearly demonstrates that histopathological mechanisms are not the primary epilepsy drivers.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the BKM120 treatment results.

claim: Acute 1 hr of BKM120 administration was sufficient to completely inhibit the increased phosphorylation levels induced by PTZ.
source: Acute 1 hr of BKM120 administration was sufficient to completely inhibit the increased phosphorylation levels induced by PTZ, notably returning mutant hippocampal mTOR-dependent pS473-AKT levels to baseline untreated control levels.
evidence: This claim is supported by RPPA data in Figure 8.

claim: BKM120 treatment normalized the PTZ-seizure induction threshold, despite continued dysplasia in Nestin-cre;E545K mutants.
source: This was sufficient to normalize the PTZ-seizure induction threshold, despite continued dysplasia in Nestin-cre;E545K mutants.
evidence: This claim is supported by seizure data in Figure 7.

claim: Elevated PI3K signaling is itself actively epileptogenic, independent of underlying developmental pathology.
source: We conclude that elevated PI3K signaling is itself actively epileptogenic, independent of underlying developmental pathology.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the combined seizure and signaling data.

claim: The discovery that Pik3ca-related epilepsy is independent of dysplasia and susceptible to acute modulation is a major and paradigm shifting finding.
source: The discovery that Pik3ca-related epilepsy is independent of dysplasia and susceptible to acute modulation is a major and paradigm shifting finding.
evidence: This is an interpretive statement about the significance of the findings.

claim: The mouse models represent surrogates for the entire group of patients with segmental brain overgrowth, including patients with somatic mosaic mTOR and AKT3 mutations.
source: Since PIK3CA resides at the top of the PI3K-AKT pathway, our mouse models represent surrogates for the entire group of patients with segmental brain overgrowth, including patients with somatic mosaic mTOR and AKT3 mutations (Keppler-Noreuil et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2012; D'Gama et al., 2015; Conway et al., 2007; Jansen et al., 2015; Mirzaa et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the pathway position of PIK3CA and comparison to human disorders.

claim: SEGCD is associated with early onset, severe and frequently intractable epilepsy that responds poorly to standard seizure medications.
source: SEGCD is associated with early onset, severe and frequently intractable epilepsy that responds poorly to standard seizure medications (Bast et al., 2006; Fauser et al., 2015; Fauser, 2006; Pasquier et al., 2002; Russo et al., 2003; Tassi, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on SEGCD epilepsy.

claim: Epilepsy surgery has been comparatively more successful (73%) in combating seizures in SEGCD children.
source: Epilepsy surgery has been comparatively more successful (73%) in combating seizures in the same children (Fauser et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature on surgical outcomes.

claim: A drug-based therapy would clearly be preferable to epilepsy surgery.
source: A drug-based therapy however, would clearly be preferable.
evidence: This is a value judgment based on general medical principles.

claim: mTOR inhibition with rapamycin has shown therapeutic promise in FCD patients and animals models.
source: mTOR inhibition with rapamycin has shown therapeutic promise in FCD patients and animals models (Baek et al., 2015; Curatolo and Moavero, 2013; Lim et al., 2015; Moon et al., 2015); however, rapamycin treatments are not acute.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature on rapamycin treatment.

claim: Rapamycin treatments are not acute.
source: mTOR inhibition with rapamycin has shown therapeutic promise in FCD patients and animals models (Baek et al., 2015; Curatolo and Moavero, 2013; Lim et al., 2015; Moon et al., 2015); however, rapamycin treatments are not acute.
evidence: This claim is based on knowledge of rapamycin pharmacology.

claim: Acute small molecule-based modulation of PI3K signaling, despite the presence of dysplasia, has dramatic therapeutic benefit.
source: Our data demonstrates that acute small molecule-based modulation of PI3K signaling, despite the presence of dysplasia, has dramatic therapeutic benefit.
evidence: This claim is based on the BKM120 treatment data.
